senses.gloss: f. (denom. of נָזִיר or נָזַר) abstinence, esp. the Nazarite’s vow, nazariteship. Sifra Emor, ch. III, Par. 4 (ref. to Lev. XXII, 2 וינזרו) אין נזירה אלא הפרשה the verb nazar means to abstain (guard); Num. R. s. 10 אין נזירות … אלא פרישות; Yalk. Lev. 632; Sifra l. c. הא אין נזירות וכ׳.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 10:7">Num. R. s. 10</cite> <he>אדם קובע עליו נזירות בתוך נְזִירָתוֹ</he> a person may take the Nazarite’s vow within the time of his vow.

<cite ref="Mishnah Nazir 4:7">Naz. IV, 7</cite> <he>מגלח על נזירות אביו</he> may cut his hair (and sacrifice at the expiration of his vow) on the nazariteship of his (deceased) father, i.e. use his father’s money set apart for the purpose.

<cite ref="Mishnah Nazir 4:7">Ib.</cite> <he>הפריש … לנְזִירָתוֹ</he> (Rashi to ib. 30ᵃ; <cite ref="N00452"><he>נְזִירוּת</he></cite>) he had set apart money for his nazaritic expenses without mentioning special items; Tosef. ib. III, 16; <cite ref="Tosefta Meilah 1:9">Tosef. Meïl. I, 9</cite>.

<cite ref="Nedarim 3b:1">Ned. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>הנ׳ חל על הנ׳</he> (sub. <cite ref="N00240"><he>נֵדֶר</he></cite>) one nazaritic vow may take effect on top of another, i.e. a vow taken within the term of another, takes effect when the first expires, v. supra; a. fr.—Pl. (of <cite ref="N00452"><he>נְזִירָה</he></cite>) <cite ref="N00452"><he>נְזִירוֹת</he></cite>, (of <cite ref="N00452"><he>נְזִירוּת</he></cite>) <he>נְזִירִיּוֹת</he>.
Ned. I, 1 נ׳ כנ׳ (כינויי) the substitutes for nazir are as effective as the word nazir itself. Tosef. Naz. l. c. לשאר נְזִירוֹתָיו for his other nazaritic expenses.
<cite ref="Nazir 14b:9">Naz. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>שתי נ׳</he> two nazaritic vows. Y. ib. V, end, 54ᵇ <he>וכולן … נזיריות</he> and all of them must observe nine nazaritic vows in succession; a. fr.
